hints: Ask yourself, is leukaemia a normal immune response to infection, or is it uncontrolled cell division (cancer)? Focus on the word leukaemia.
Recall where all lymphocytes are first made, and think about what happens when that production loses control of mitosis.
walkthrough:
**Remember what leukaemia really is**

Think of leukaemia not as an infection, but as a cancer of white blood cells. That means the high count is not because the body needs more defence, it is because division has gone out of control.

**Link to where white cells are made**

All lymphocytes (both B and T types) are produced by stem cells dividing in the bone marrow. In leukaemia, these marrow cells divide by uncontrolled mitosis, so huge numbers of abnormal lymphocytes are released into the blood.

**Check the options against this idea**

Options A and D say more cells are required, which sounds like a normal immune response. That is not correct here. Option C puts production in the plasma, which is just the fluid part of blood, not a production site. Only B correctly names uncontrolled production in bone marrow.

options.A: The increase is not a useful response to make more antibodies. Leukaemic cells are abnormal and do not function normally.
options.B: Correct. Leukaemia is uncontrolled mitosis of lymphocyte precursors in bone marrow, so many extra (often immature) lymphocytes enter the blood.
options.C: Memory cells are not produced in plasma. Plasma is the fluid carrying blood cells, while lymphocytes are made in bone marrow and mature in lymphoid tissue.
options.D: The body is not deliberately making more T-lymphocytes to help. The high count is due to cancerous overproduction, not a controlled need.
